verification-preview-process-ownershipverification-addressing-and-errors0 of 0.375 (minor)failThe verifier reserves an ephemeral port with freePort and starts the preview with --strictPort. The child&#39;s own announcement of its address is never read. Readiness polling is not raced against the child&#39;s exit. engineering-preview-terminated-on-every-exitengineering-verification-tooling-robustness0.625 of 0.625 (major)passstartPreview launches Vite&#39;s own bin directly with node, so there is no npm or npx wrapper. It runs as a detached process group, and stop() sends SIGTERM to the whole group (-pid), awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; promise, then escalates to SIGKILL and awaits again. When readiness times out, startPreview calls stop() itself before throwing. In verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs, both the repository copies and the bootstrap template copies, main() assigns `preview` inside try and runs `await browser?.close().catch(()=&gt;{}); await preview?.stop()` in finally. Every path the guidance names goes through that finally: success (return 0), a failing check or later error (catch, return 1), and a chromium.launch() failure (thrown after preview is set). The bootstrap preview.mjs is the same code (detached, process.kill(-pid), awaited exit). E2E-001/E2E-002 check that no preview is still listening after a passing run and after render faults. I am ruling with judges A and B. Judge C fails it because the SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers call process.exit(130) and skip the finally block. The code does show that, but signal-driven termination is not one of the exit paths the guidance names (success, a failing check, a browser launch failure, an error after the preview started), and the rules forbid failing on an unnamed scenario. scripts/lib/preview.mjs:88 stop() returns early when the child has not yet emitted 'exit'. If the preview process spawn fails (e.g. ENOENT), child.pid is undefined, so process.kill(-undefined) throws and is silently swallowed. The `exit` promise never resolves for a spawn error because only the 'exit' event is listened to (not 'error'), so `await exit` after SIGKILL hangs forever. Also, the 'error' event on the child is unhandled, which crashes the process.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/verify.mjs:119 Error checking happens only after settle+readStep for each step, but console/page errors are collected asynchronously. For the initial step, errors raised before the page stabilizes are checked, but the first-step check occurs only after SETTLE_MS. More importantly, a failing step transition where waitForFunction times out reports `reported()` only as a suffix; fine. In verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs, both the repository copies and the bootstrap template copies, main() assigns `preview` inside try and runs `await browser?.close().catch(()=&gt;{}); await preview?.stop()` in finally. In verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs, both the repository copies and the bootstrap template copies, main() assigns `preview` inside try and runs `await browser?.close().catch(()=&gt;{}); await preview?.stop()` in finally. The bootstrap preview.mjs is the same code (detached, process.kill(-pid), awaited exit). E2E-001/E2E-002 check that no preview is still listening after a passing run and after render faults. I am ruling with judges A and B. Judge C fails it because the SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers call process.exit(130) and skip the finally block. The code does show that, but signal-driven termination is not one of the exit paths the guidance names (success, a failing check, a browser launch failure, an error after the preview started), and the rules forbid failing on an unnamed scenario. They assert on exit code, stdout/stderr, manifest.json and screenshot pixels only after that has resolved, so they wait on observable state. Inside the scripts, each step advance waits on data-step-index with page.waitForFunction (a polling wait with a timeout) before anything is read. The only waitForTimeout in tests/ is a no-op stub in the mocked page of verify-script.test.ts, and the only setTimeout is inside a string injected as a page-error fault. I am ruling with judges A and B. Judge C fails it on the scripts&#39; settle delays (inspect&#39;s --settle waitForTimeout and verify&#39;s settle()). Those delays belong to the product under test, not to the tests. INT-002 deliberately tests that inspect waits its settle interval (capturedAt - navigatedAt &gt;= SETTLE). Both scripts wait for the step-index state before settling. The guidance also calls fixed settle delays validator noise. It runs as a detached process group, and stop() sends SIGTERM to the whole group (-pid), awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; promise, then escalates to SIGKILL and awaits again. When readiness times out, startPreview calls stop() itself before throwing. In verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs, both the repository copies and the bootstrap template copies, main() assigns `preview` inside try and runs `await browser?.close().catch(()=&gt;{}); await preview?.stop()` in finally. Every path the guidance names goes through that finally: success (return 0), a failing check or later error (catch, return 1), and a chromium.launch() failure (thrown after preview is set). The bootstrap preview.mjs is the same code (detached, process.kill(-pid), awaited exit). E2E-001/E2E-002 check that no preview is still listening after a passing run and after render faults. I am ruling with judges A and B. Judge C fails it because the SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers call process.exit(130) and skip the finally block. The code does show that, but signal-driven termination is not one of the exit paths the guidance names (success, a failing check, a browser launch failure, an error after the preview started), and the rules forbid failing on an unnamed scenario. None of them sleeps for a fixed time. Every browser run goes through sandbox `run()`, which resolves only on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event (sandbox.ts:14-23). Each assertion then reads the exit code, the output or the manifest written by a process that has already finished. None of these tests calls waitForTimeout, setTimeout as a delay, or a sleep. The only `setTimeout` in verify.test.ts (line 116) is text inside an injected fault string that gets written into the sample. The only `waitForTimeout` in tests/ is a no-op `async () =&gt; {}` on the mocked page in the unit test (verify-script.test.ts:110), so it does not wait for anything. In that mock, step advancement goes through a waitForFunction stub that checks the index (lines 116-118). Where the scripts move between steps, they first wait on observable state: `waitForFunction` polls data-step-index with a timeout (verify.mjs:110-117, inspect-presentation.mjs:257) before reading or capturing. Those are in the delivered verify and inspect tools, not in the tests. They run only after the state wait on data-step-index has confirmed the step, so they do not replace waiting for state. The test&#39;s own `--settle 1700` (inspect.test.ts:15,26) sets a capture-settle option that the test checks as a product behaviour (lines 75-79). It is not a sleep the test uses before asserting a step. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[],"verification-tooling":[],"engineering-quality":[{"id":"engineering-bootstrap-scripts-generic","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The auditor says all three clauses are met, but the second clause fails. That clause requires the template scripts to reject an unregistered slug with a clear non-zero failure &quot;rather than timing out&quot;. The template inspect script never checks the slug against the registry. It opens the route and waits up to 8000 ms for `[data-step-count]`. Only when that wait expires does it throw PhaseError, and even then the message only asks &quot;(is the slug registered?)&quot;. So the rejection depends on the timeout, which is exactly the behaviour the requirement rules out. The auditor admits the detection mechanism is the 8 s selector wait. Wrapping that timeout in a readable message and exiting 1 does not change the fact that the slug is caught by timing out, not by a registry check. The criterion asks that every readiness wait has a timeout, and the readiness wait in both preview.mjs copies has one: a 30s default deadline loop. When the loop runs out, it stops the preview and throws a PhaseError. The auditor&#39;s point is that one fetch() inside probe() has no abort signal. That defeats the verdict only if a probe to the local vite preview stalls with no response, and the material never shows that happening. The review guidance does not name that scenario, and the judging rules say not to fail a criterion on a hypothetical input the guidance does not name. Node&#39;s built-in fetch also has its own connect and header timeouts (Node behaviour, not shown in the material), so even a stalled probe would not hang forever. The auditor also agrees that the build-before-preview clause is met (verify awaits runBuild before startPreview) and that the ready-URL parsing clause does not apply, since readiness probes over HTTP instead of parsing printed output. So all three clauses are met and the pass stands.","evidence":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs and the template copy: startPreview sets `const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs` (timeoutMs = 30_000), loops `while (Date.now() &lt; deadline)`, and after the loop calls `aw…","probe() is `const res = await fetch(url); return res.ok` inside a try/catch. It calls the local 127.0.0.1 preview, and the material shows no case where that call stalls.","scripts/verify.mjs and the template copy: main awaits `runBuild(root)` before `startPreview(root)`. inspect-presentation.mjs awaits runBuild when it builds, and otherwise uses an existing dist.","Readiness is detected by an HTTP probe, not by parsing printed output, so the ANSI and chunk-split parsing clause does not apply.","The review guidance fails a wait only when it &#39;has no timeout&#39;. It does not name a per-probe abort for a server that never responds."],"citations":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/preview.mjs","scripts/verify.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":2,"sample":3}],"testing-evidence":[],"assumption-handling":[]}
